title: Compatibility of the Legendary Weapons
text: “A rabbit spirit, is it? Rabbits are my exclusive patent! I shall not lose, I say!”
I would charm Father as an usaunny!
“This guy’s still competing! I really wish he’d knock it off already.”
“Hmph. What exactly can you do? Go on, show me if you’ve got it in you, indeed.”
“There’s really no need to fight over this, you know. Though… I suppose reporting you to that girl who flew the nest of the main timeline you’re so afraid of is always an option.”
At those words, Big Sister rose up in my mind.
“Not that Boku lacks aptitude as a hammer spirit either, you know. Helping beat you into a pulp… that Boku could probably manage.”
Hammer… Big Sister’s formidable figure came flooding back to me. Being the kind of person who could serve as Filo-tan’s big sister, she really was a terrifying one, I say.
“Gah… what is this?! Relying on Big Sister is downright cowardly, I say!”
As I pointed at the strange spirit, the spear spirit let out a bitter laugh.
“So, who do you think he is? Care to guess?”
“Because—! You already know this guy misses every single time!”
“I do not know, indeed! Is it the Mole? Or perhaps, judging by that tone, Itsuki got promoted from riska to spirit!”
“Comparing Boku to that sarcastic bastard is the height of humiliation! Do you have any idea how much trouble Boku went through?!”
What a noisy, squawking spirit, I say.
“Fine, Boku will say it before the day’s over. Boku is Theodore!”
“Theodore… who might that be, indeed?”
“Ehhh… this guy… already forgot?!”
Who was that again? Only a hazy impression floated up.
“Well, he was usually called by his nickname more often anyway. Once you misremember someone under a different name, that’s all that comes to mind after that.”
“Ahh, honestly… thanks to that, Boku ended up like this, and it’s humiliating enough as it is! Too much trouble, so Boku’s done dealing with him.”
With that! The spirit went flying off toward the other spirits. Seen from a distance, it looked as if she were trying to take charge of the discussion.
“It’s not that you can’t remember—it seems you’ve simply filed him under a different name, Motoyasu Kitamura.”
“So who is it, indeed?”
“Would ‘Theo’ ring a bell? No, wait—in your case, I believe you filed him under Rabbit Guy.”
“Rabbit Guy, is it?”
It surfaced in my mind with a puff.
“Was that fellow a spirit-type all along, indeed?”
“Well, ‘close but not quite’ would be the honest answer— he was a bit diluted, but this loop brought out all sorts of things. Even this side found a few surprising elements in it, you know.”
“What is it, indeed?”

“Hmm… honestly, it’s not something you or he really need to know, but leaving it vague would probably itch at you, so I’ll explain… his soul was quite special. Ah, though the him of now has already split off, so to speak—reentered the cycle of reincarnation—so he’s a separate existence at this point.”
Already at this stage I hadn’t the faintest idea what was going on, I say.
“To put it simply for you… his was a soul that had a spirit-type as a past life, I suppose you could say.”
“Does that mean something, indeed?”
“Well, for one, it makes becoming a Hero more likely, but there’s also that technology that came to light this loop, right? The one the Rumo-species you call Mole was researching.”
Hearing that, it came back to me. Ah, right, there had been such a thing. Rafumi had been analyzing it.

“There’s a technology that existed in the past, but was lost because of the bastard who wrecked this world to pieces. Back in my own lifetime it was called ‘Harmonize’ or ‘Synchro’—a technique for raising the power of both a spirit-type and their contractor.”
Why did the explanation about Rabbit Guy turn into an explanation of this technology, indeed? As I tilted my head, the spear spirit sighed and continued further.

“Just because the technology was lost doesn’t mean its very existence vanished completely. What mattered most was that his soul—and his body too, originally—carried the right factor for it. He was an all-attribute type who could Harmonize with any spirit-type or person. So while taking part in the research, power given to him by other spirit-types accumulated in his vessel, and after death, it let him take shape as a spirit like this.”
Though he’s a mixed spirit, blended together like a mixed fruit juice. The spear spirit seemed to think that explanation had been sufficient.
“There’s a compatibility involved in why I chose you as my holder. Your past life has nothing to do with spirit-types, mind you. In my case, I simply happen to be well-suited to types like you.”
Rather sarcastically self-deprecating about it, he was… should I be angry about that, indeed?
“The conversation’s jumping around so much I haven’t a clue, indeed.”

“I suppose it did jump around a bit—call it a digression on top of a digression? Anyway, once you get to the class of Legendary Weapon spirits, compatibility with the holder matters. It’s necessary for holding me properly. Otherwise the strain falls on this side, and I can’t draw out the power for you well.”
Did this tie back into my own situation somehow, indeed?

“Comparisons don’t mean all that much, but, well—Ren Amaki, the Sword Hero, might be the easiest example. The sword-type Legendary Weapon has a distinctive set of values, and when someone who fits those values holds it, its output comes out far greater.”

Was that so, indeed? Now that I thought about it, across the loops so far, Ren’s strength—or rather the power of his skills—did seem to fluctuate somewhat. Perhaps that was due to variation across the loops, differences in personality causing differences in output.

“Of course, there’s also the nobility and various other factors that we Legendary Weapon spirits select for, you understand? That said, those rotten souls you all call reincarnators are out of the question entirely. Forcing us onto holders like that puts a massive strain on us.”

Pretty much outright torture that could genuinely wear someone down, that. Complaining in that manner, he seemed to be laying bare the inner workings of the Legendary Weapons and the Seven Star Weapons.
“We call our holders Heroes for a reason. There’s no way someone without courage could bear to hold us.”
Though the shape and direction of that varies by each individual spirit, he added as a supplement. These spirits really did seem to be a troublesome bunch in all sorts of ways.

“In the previous world, Itsuki Kawasumi, the Bow Hero—he’s a good example. Even after his ideology and the shape of his soul changed, he still fought to protect others. Even in the dark, even in despair, he never lost his light.”
That quick-to-act, always-attacking-first Itsuki, was it, indeed.

“If a rotten soul found himself in the same situation as him—could he challenge someone stronger than himself, with no hope of winning, just to protect another? Could those bastards keep walking forward through that kind of sacrifice, wearing themselves down to nothing?”
“I see. Doubtful, indeed.”

I don’t recall which loop it was, but those are the type who can’t endure even a short stretch before rushing off for revenge and getting cut down for their trouble. I’d heard that the Itsuki of that world was prepared to keep fighting for years, decades even—right up until the very day he died, whenever that day came. He’d been fired up about dragging as many villains down with him as possible. I remembered it well, since Father had been quite worried and considerate about it at the time.

“Truth be told, we spirits properly explained to our chosen Heroes—through the system—how to draw out each of our powers in accordance with the world’s laws. But somewhere amid the long years of fighting, the mastermind behind the Waves had planted something, and at the eleventh hour it caused insufficient explanations and connection failures. I was genuinely alarmed, I’ll tell you that.”
“What exactly does that mean, indeed? No… could it be—”
Suddenly, memories of what happened on Cal Mira Island back in the very first world came flooding back to me.

“Oh? So you can actually follow along, can you. That’s right… the reason we couldn’t share the reinforcement methods across the multiple overlapping worlds, even though we should’ve been able to, was because of that. That mastermind who called herself a goddess, falsely claiming godhood—she was frighteningly thorough. I was genuinely rattled.”
It seemed the real body of the Crimson Swine had been rigging all sorts of things behind the scenes, indeed.
“What does that mean?! Spell it out in more detail, indeed!”
“It’s all over and done with now, and the reconnection went smoothly, so I don’t think you really need to worry about it? Consider it a digression, if you like.”
“Just tell me already, indeed.”

“Well, if you insist. Amid all the various events and battles that happened before the Waves occurred, it seems she’d rigged the Legendary Weapons and Seven Star Weapons to malfunction. When I looked into it, I found it had even been rigged at the moment you were stabbed—a double blow. The same was true for the others as well.”
Ugh… I felt a phantom stab of pain shoot through my side. So there had been a scheme in place to keep me from drawing out the weapon’s full power at the moment I was stabbed, had there, indeed?

“It seems she’d rigged all sorts of things—the opponents fought when your previous holder was being selected, things placed inside the spear, all manner of objects. Apparently infection even occurred during clashes with reincarnators or those under their influence. It didn’t even need to be through outright theft to get planted in… She was maneuvering behind the scenes through every trick imaginable, and it was an absolute nightmare to deal with.”

So she’d been planting things since even before my time, back when someone else held the spear. Just how far had the real body of the Crimson Swine gone with her schemes, indeed? Perhaps that level of thoroughness had been necessary for her plans. Either way, what absolute garbage, I say.
